name: walk-mobile-hud
description: Walk-mode HUD on a real phone viewport. MUST be run with SHOT_TOUCH=1 — `(pointer: coarse)` is what `WalkHud` branches on, and without it the app renders the DESKTOP hint bar at phone width, which is not what this scenario audits. The guard step below fails loudly rather than let that happen silently again (v0.31.8.91).

steps.name: phone-viewport
steps.failMessage: this scenario is named for the MOBILE walk HUD but had no viewport step, so it screenshotted at desktop width and never audited the mobile HUD at all (v0.31.8.90). `resize_window` clamps at ~606px, so a true phone width needs a `viewport` step.

steps.name: require-touch-emulation
steps.eval: (()=>{ if (!window.matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches) throw new Error('run with SHOT_TOUCH=1: without it WalkHud renders the DESKTOP hint bar and this scenario audits the wrong branch') })()

steps.name: dismiss-overlays
steps.eval: try { localStorage.setItem('hdb_onboarded','1') } catch {}; const s = window.__store.getState(); s.endTour?.(); s.setOnboardingOpen?.(false); s.dismissLocationPrompt?.()

steps.name: enter-walk-overlay-shown
steps.failMessage: 'Entering walkthrough' splash never appeared, so the gone-wait below would pass vacuously. If this transition genuinely raises no splash (same mode, or the room editor owns the overlay) delete BOTH guard steps rather than widening the timeout.

steps.name: enter-walk-overlay-gone
steps.failMessage: 'Entering walkthrough' splash still up; the next screenshot would capture the splash, not the scene. See docs/visual-verification-playbook.md.
